understanding.goal_understanding: The objective was to complete each level by placing all selectable pieces onto the goal tiles marked with '+' on the grid. If there were multiple '+' tiles, every one had to be occupied at the same time by a selectable piece for the level to register WIN, and finishing the final WIN ends the whole game.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: A single piece is 'selected' at a time. CLICKing a target grid coordinate attempts to move the selected piece directly to that square (effectively a teleport/relocation attempt), but the move fails if the destination is blocked/illegal (e.g., wall/obstacle or otherwise not a valid landing tile). MOVE_RIGHT (and presumably other cardinal move actions) attempts to shift the selected piece by one tile in that direction, but movement is prevented by walls/obstacles/boundaries; when blocked, the piece stays in place and the step is still consumed. Each action spends 1 step from a finite per-level budget, so inefficient back-and-forth moves can exhaust the budget before reaching the goal configuration.
